model: Regulated utility dividend discount on adjusted EPS at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Low end of management's 7-9% long-term adjusted EPS growth target, cross-checked against the 9.2% five-year equity CAGR and ~11% guided rate-base CAGR (equity growth overstates per-share growth because part of it is new share issuance and NCI).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (9-10%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.8% 5yr, -1.7% 3yr) and GAAP EPS (negative). Revenue is distorted by pass-through gas costs; GAAP EPS by the FY2020 discontinued-operations gain (EPS split-adjusted 2:1, Aug 2023) and FY2025 one-offs ($464M Track 2 disallowance, SI Partners sale tax charges). Equity is total equity including NCI.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported FCF is negative in every year FY2018-FY2025. SBC ($64-86M) is immaterial against capex of $8-10B.

scenario_narratives.base: Base: FY2026 adjusted EPS lands at $5.25 (high end of $4.80-5.30 guidance after the Q3 beat on Oncor). FY2027 $5.30, low-to-mid of the $5.10-5.70 range because the pending CPUC proposed decision on the 2024 GRC attrition mechanism (~$188M revenue requirement) is assumed only partly mitigated. 2028-2030 compound 8-9% on the ~11% rate-base CAGR to ~$6.77 in FY2030, the low end of management's $6.70-7.50 outlook (haircut for regulatory lag and financing cost). The dividend grows ~2-3.5%/yr while the $65B plan is funded, so payout falls from 50% to ~44% by 2030, then rebuilds to 65% by 2035 as EPS growth fades to 3.5%. Terminal 3% growth at 65% payout implies ~9% incremental ROE, under the 9.75-10% allowed returns.
scenario_narratives.bull: Bull: Texas does the work. Oncor's capital plan steps up again (765-kV backbone, Batch Zero large-load interconnections all land in rate base under the UTM with little lag), FY2027 comes in at $5.55, and 10%/yr compounding reaches ~$7.40 in FY2030, the upper part of the $6.70-7.50 outlook. California stays merely neutral: the CPUC attrition correction is granted or mitigated and no wildfire loss exceeds insurance plus the Wildfire Fund. Port Arthur Phase 1 and ECA reach COD on schedule so the retained 25% of SI Partners distributes cash. Growth fades from 8.5% to 4.5% by 2035, terminal 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Bear: California is the axis. The CPUC proposed decision stands (FY2027 at $5.10, the low end), further GRC disallowances follow the $651M Track 2 precedent, and a Palisades/Eaton or Norte Fire liability lands partly unrecovered under inverse condemnation, pushing a ratings downgrade that raises debt cost and forces more ATM equity at a lower price. EPS compounds only 5%/yr to ~$5.90 in FY2030, well short of the $6.70 floor of the outlook, the dividend grows 2%, and growth fades to 2.5%. No solvency event is assumed: the Wildfire Fund and the 2025 Continuation Account hold.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sempra is valued as what an owner receives: a dividend funded by regulated earnings, with retained earnings reinvested into rate base at allowed returns. Adjusted EPS guidance (FY2026 high end of $4.80-5.30, FY2027 $5.10-5.70, FY2030 $6.70-7.50) anchors the path, haircut to the low end in the base case; the payout stays depressed through the $65B plan and rebuilds as growth fades. Discounted at an 8% cost of equity with the terminal dividend capped at 20x (13x earnings), below where regulated utilities usually trade, so the model does not rely on multiple expansion. A 15% hurdle is not a realistic ask of a regulated utility; the entry price will sit far below the market price by construction.
key_risks_to_valuation: Wildfire liability under inverse condemnation (Palisades/Eaton against SoCalGas, Norte Fire against SDG&E): a loss beyond insurance and the Wildfire Fund is not modelled as a discrete charge, only as slower bear-case growth
CPUC disallowances and lag: the pending attrition-mechanism decision (~$188M) and the $651M Track 2 precedent
Cost-of-equity sensitivity: a long-duration dividend stream; +/-1pt on the 8% rate moves value by roughly 20-25%
Dilution: per-share growth assumes ATM issuance stays within plan; a downgrade or a failed KKR close (termination fee aside) would force more equity
Terminal payout: value is sensitive to the 65% payout / 3% growth pairing, which presumes ~9% incremental ROE persists
FY0 adjusted EPS is estimated and the end-of-year timing convention understates value by ~6-7%

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 76.21-101.04
data_sources.financials: SRE_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL); Q3-2026 10-Q for share count, Sempra shareholders' equity ($33,327M), debt and cash at 2026-09-30; FY2025 10-K for dividends, SBC, buybacks; segment earnings from the kpis table
data_sources.qualitative: SRE_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): guidance as of the Q3-2026 release (2026-11-05), capital plan, KKR/SI Partners sale, wildfire and CPUC matters

inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 diluted weighted-average (655.939M; treasury-stock effect of RSUs and the two unsettled ATM forward sale agreements, ~5.0M shares). Cover count 654.12M at 2026-11-02. Held flat because the driver is adjusted EPS, which already carries future ATM/forward dilution; the per-share value is invariant to the count on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow add-back ($64M). Already expensed inside adjusted earnings, so the forward SBC row is held at 0% to avoid charging it twice; house and street coincide.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 8.0% rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: USD risk-free ~4.3% (10-year Treasury) + ~0.75 regulated-utility beta x 5.0% ERP = ~8.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios; wildfire, CPUC and execution risk are charged once, in the flows and the weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: adjusted earnings are after all lease cost and interest; lease liabilities ($2.6B) are not deducted again.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once: the flow is adjusted earnings attributable to common shares, i.e. after NCI (KKR/ADIA in SI Partners, Blackstone in Port Arthur Phase 2, TTI/others in Oncor Holdings) and including the 80.25% Oncor equity earnings. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: On this route last_fcf is the FY2025 common dividend (~$2.58/sh x ~653M sh), the equity flow the model discounts; it is NOT reported_fcf - sbc - interest. Reported FCF (OCF 4,565 - capex 10,612 = -6,047) is structurally negative in a rate-base capex supercycle and is not a valuation input.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt held at zero in the model because the discounted flow is post-interest and to equity. Actual consolidated debt at 2026-09-30: short-term 4,438 + current LTD 1,528 + LTD and finance leases 31,508 = 37,474; cash 34. Oncor's debt is off balance sheet (equity method).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: dividend discount on adjusted EPS, capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero. Owner-FCF DCF was rejected: (1) consolidated FCF has been negative every year since 2018 (-$6.0B FY2025) because rate-base capex is debt/equity funded by design, (2) the largest growth asset, 80.25% of Oncor, is equity-accounted and absent from consolidated EBITDA, capex and debt, (3) SI Partners is about to fall from control to a 25% minority stake (KKR sale, ~$9.99B, expected to close November 2026), so consolidated flows break at the close, and (4) NCI leakage is large. Sum-of-parts was considered and not used: all three segments produce the same kind of flow (regulated or long-term-contracted post-interest earnings), management guides on consolidated adjusted EPS through 2030, and post-sale ~95% of earnings are regulated, so segment multiples would add false precision; the segment mix is expressed in the scenario growth paths instead. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = adjusted earnings to common (adjusted EPS x 655.9M); EBITDA margin 100%; SBC, D&A, tax 0 (all inside earnings); 'capex %' = retention ratio, so the FCF row is the common dividend; terminal cap multiple is a multiple of the terminal DIVIDEND (20x at 65% payout = 13x P/E). FY0 CAVEAT: FY2025 adjusted EPS of ~$4.65 is an estimate (GAAP $2.75 plus the $464M after-tax GRC Track 2 disallowance and the SI Partners held-for-sale deferred-tax charges; the adjusted figure is in the 8-K release, not the 10-K). It affects nothing downstream: year-1 growth is set so FY2026 equals guidance. TIMING: end-of-year discounting from FY0=FY2025 treats the FY2026 dividend as a year away when the year is 87% elapsed, which understates value by roughly 6-7%; kept for comparability with the rest of the folder. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours. Buybacks ($58M FY2025) are tax-withholding repurchases only; Sempra is a net issuer via the ATM.
inputs.band_note: House/street band collapses: SBC is expensed inside adjusted EPS on both bases.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: roughly half of earnings depend on a single increasingly adversarial regulator (CPUC), wildfire exposure is strict-liability with three open matters (Palisades, Eaton, Norte), and both rating agencies are on negative outlook. Base 50%: guidance has been met or beaten and is reaffirmed through 2030. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs Oncor capex upside, timely Texas recovery, a benign California outcome and on-schedule LNG CODs all at once.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
